candidates.label: Pool of Bethesda
candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate for the Pool of Bethesda matches OpenBible.info's independently recorded point for the same site exactly, and the location corresponds to the excavated twin-pool remains near St. Anne's Church.

summary.text: The Pool of Bethesda is a reservoir near Jerusalem's Sheep Gate that the Gospel of John names as the site where Jesus healed a man who had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.

history.text: Archaeological excavation near St. Anne's Church uncovered a large twin-pool complex divided by a central dam, with column bases and sockets marking five porticoes, matching the Gospel of John's description and confirming the pool's existence as a real Second Temple-period structure.

scripture.textWEB: Now in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches.

politicalHistory.note: Augustus did not grant Archelaus the royal title his father's will asked for, only "ethnarch."

politicalHistory.entity: Roman province of Judea (ruler: Prefects, e.g. Pontius Pilate)
politicalHistory.note: Quirinius, governing Syria, conducted a census at the start of this period. Luke 2:1-2 is dated by some instead to the time of Herod's birth narrative, before 4 BC, rather than to Quirinius's AD 6 census; this note does not resolve the question.
